rationale: The workflow repeatedly fetches Node.js dependencies via `npm i` in docs/ on every push to dev and every manual dispatch, with no existing dependency cache. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (cache dependency downloads) is supported by measured evidence showing modest aggregate CI savings, and its preconditions are met: repeated dependency fetching is measurable and the cache key can include the dependency manifest (docs/package.json, which exists in the repository). No contraindication applies: there is no equivalent cache already present, and the npm cache is trusted, input-keyed content that does not alter build integrity. Adding an actions/cache@v4 step keyed on docs/package.json before dependency installation preserves all build and deployment steps, required checks, permissions, and concurrency behavior, while reducing repeated network fetches on warm runs. Other patterns were rejected: P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE is contraindicated for deployment work, P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW lacks a verified repository omission policy, and P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT lacks representative successful-duration history for this workflow.
